latest_final:
The apparent crisis was a deliberate wordplay: the “courses” that vanished were not university classes but the food courses of a formal hall dinner (“high table dinner”), and “choosing courses before the deadline” alluded to selecting dishes for the meal.

On that evening the student attended the high table dinner and personally did a physical, ordinary-seeming action involving the food or drink being consumed at the table. That action was enough of a breach of the dinner’s expected etiquette that the serving staff responded by clearing the courses away. As a result, the dishes that were meant for the student never reached them, so all of “their courses” were gone within that single evening.

The explicit “no” answers rule out the ordinary academic explanations (system removal, other students taking places, missed deadline, account access, device damage) as well as the more specific meal explanations that were tested — being finished eating, leaving the seat, a formal tradition, cutlery signals, toasts, passing drinks, serving others, choking or spilling. What remains established is that the student was a diner at a high table dinner, consumed food or drink there, took a physical action they thought was harmless, and that action led the staff to clear the courses, leaving the student with none.
